docs.t: About Dlonem — a one-person studio in Virginia
docs.x: About One person, one made-up word Dlonem is a one-person studio. The apps, the mods, the videos and the Discord servers are all built and supported by the same person. Home › About Who this is I’m Thomas. Dlonem LLC is my studio, and for most practical purposes Dlonem LLC is me. I write the code, draw the icons, record the videos, and answer the support email. If you send a bug report, it lands in front of the person who caused the bug. The name is a made-up word with no meaning behind it. It came out of a random name generator years ago and stuck, which is a much less interesting origin than people expect. The full story of how I got there (by way of a Roblox account called Carlman622, a World of Warcraft warlock, and a decade as Mr.Potato) is on the Legacy page , if you want the long version. What I make Four phone apps. Three of them are Break Buddy apps, one each for cannabis, caffeine and nicotine, and they all do the same job: help you take a break from a habit and show you plainly what is happening while you do. The fourth, Tiny Dragon Hoard , is a cozy idle game about a dragon who collects things. All four are here . Two Crusader Kings III mods. The Long Night & Azor Ahai builds the Long Night out as a real endgame for the A Game of Thrones total conversion, and Supernatural adds vampires, werewolves, witches and hunters to the base game. Both are free, both are on the Steam Workshop, and both can be installed by hand without Steam . Four Discord communities and a YouTube channel. The oldest community has been running since 2016. The channel is where all of this started, and it is still the reason most people find anything else I make. Both are linked from the Community page . How I build things A few rules I hold to, because they are the reason I started making my own apps rather than using someone else’s: Your data stays on your device. The Break Buddy apps store what you enter (your history, your notes, your reminders) locally. I do not collect it and I cannot read it. The privacy policy is short because there is not much to disclose. No accounts. You should not need to sign up for anything to track your own coffee. No subscriptions. Where an app has a paid unlock, it is a one-time purchase. I am not going to charge you every month for a habit tracker. Estimates are labelled as estimates. The apps show you timelines drawn from published research, and where a number is a projection rather than a fact, it says so. These are wellness tools. They are not medical advice, and they do not claim to be. Getting in touch The fastest route depends on what you need. Each app has its own support address, listed on its policy page . For anything else, whether a bug, a question, a feature idea, or business, contact@dlonem.com reaches me. There is more detail, including what to put in a bug report so I can fix it, on the support page . For the mods specifically, the Discord servers are faster than email, because the rest of the community is there too and someone has usually hit your problem already.

It won't shame you about your coffee habit or ask for a willpower marathon, and nothing you enter ever leaves your phone. Get it on Google Play App Store — coming soon Home › Apps › Caffeine Break Buddy 12–24h After your last dose, before withdrawal starts 50% Of people get a headache in controlled studies 2–9 Days it takes, start to finish The mechanism What caffeine tolerance is Adenosine is the molecule that makes you feel sleepy. It builds up across the day and settles onto receptors that dial your alertness down. Caffeine works by blocking those receptors . It doesn't add energy so much as hide the tiredness. With daily use your body adapts. In humans, a week of 250 mg three times a day raised the density of adenosine A2A receptors on blood platelets by about 31% , and made them measurably more sensitive. In rodent brain, chronic caffeine raises A1 receptor binding by roughly 17–20% . More receptors, or more sensitive ones, means the same coffee blocks a smaller share of them. That is tolerance, and it's a physical adaptation rather than a failure of discipline. Three things most guides get wrong Nobody has measured caffeine receptor density in a living human brain. So when a site tells you your receptors reset in exactly 7, 14 or 30 days, that number is invented. The figures above come from human blood cells and from rodent brains. What has been measured in people is symptoms, and those resolve in two to nine days. Tolerance is specific to each effect. It's essentially complete for caffeine's effects on blood pressure and adrenaline within one to four days of daily use, and complete for the subjective buzz within about three weeks. But the effect on physical performance is stubborn: cyclists still got a ~4–5% power boost after 15 straight days of daily dosing. "Caffeine does nothing for regular drinkers" overstates a finding that is still contested. You don't have to be a heavy drinker. Withdrawal has been produced from as little as 100 mg a day , and after only three days of regular use. In one study of people averaging 235 mg (about two and a half cups), 52% reported moderate or severe headache when it was swapped for placebo. Hour by hour What the timeline looks like Timings vary with dose and metabolism, but the shape is consistent enough that researchers can put hours on it. 0–12 HOURS Nothing much. Caffeine's half-life is roughly three to five hours in most adults, so levels are falling but you're not empty yet. Individual values run from about two hours to ten; pregnancy and oestrogen-containing contraceptives lengthen it substantially, and smoking shortens it. 12–24 HOURS Onset. This is when it starts, and if you drink your coffee in the morning that lands squarely on the following afternoon. Headache comes first for about half of people, typically bilateral and throbbing, then fatigue and a sense of being foggy rather than tired. 20–51 HOURS The peak, and the hard part. Headache, real fatigue, low alertness, drowsiness, depressed or irritable mood, difficulty concentrating. Some people also get flu-like symptoms, nausea, or muscle stiffness. About 13% of people in controlled studies hit distress or impairment significant enough to matter at work. DAYS 3–5 It lifts. The headache is usually the first thing to go. Energy is still flat and concentration still annoying, but the trend is clearly downward. DAYS 5–9 Done, for almost everyone. The systematic review puts total duration at two to nine days, with the long tail belonging to people who were on high daily doses. AFTER If you go back, you need far less than you used to. Tolerance to the subjective effects is what fades fastest, so your old four-cup habit will hit like six. This is the part people enjoy, and the part they overshoot. The obvious question Why three apps and not one Three of these do the same job for different substances, and the reasonable question is why they are not one app with a dropdown at the top. The first reason is that the timelines are not the same shape. Caffeine clears in hours and the hard part is a few days of headaches. Nicotine's worst stretch is measured in days and the cravings outlast it by months. A cannabis tolerance break is measured in weeks, and how long it takes depends on how much was in your system to begin with. An app that tried to be all three at once would end up vague about all three, and vague is the one thing a countdown cannot afford to be. The second reason is more practical. Someone cutting back on coffee should not have to install something with a cannabis leaf on the icon, and someone quitting vapes should not have to scroll past features that have nothing to do with them. Separate apps mean each one can say exactly what it is on the home screen and nothing else. They do share an engine underneath. A fix to how a streak survives a bad day, or to how the recovery curve handles a slip, gets made once and rolls out to all three. That is why they tend to update within days of each other. This is not a feature I am saving for later; there is nothing to sign into because there is no server to sign into. Your data stays on the phone. What you log is written to your device and read back from your device. It is not uploaded, synced or analysed, which is also why losing the phone loses the history — an honest trade I would rather state plainly than hide. They work with no signal. On a plane, in a basement, with the phone in airplane mode: the timers still run and the history still opens. Nothing is a subscription. Where there is something to buy it is a one-time unlock that stays unlocked. I am not going to charge you every year to keep looking at your own data. The privacy policies spell out the specifics for each app, and they are short, because there is not much to disclose. docs.t: Nicotine Withdrawal Timeline — Nicotine Break Buddy
docs.x: Nicotine Break Buddy Watch your body heal, day by day One calm quit app for cigarettes, vapes, pouches and dip. An honest timeline of what withdrawal does, no shame about slips, and nothing you enter ever leaves your phone. Get it on Google Play App Store — coming soon Free. Optional $9.99 one-time unlock, never a subscription Home › Apps › Nicotine Break Buddy 8 days Where most unaided quit attempts fail 2–4 Weeks until most symptoms are gone 6–12 Weeks for brain receptors to reach non-smoker levels The mechanism What nicotine did to your brain, and what undoes it Nicotine binds nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (chiefly the α4β2 subtype) and leaves them desensitised. Your brain compensates by building more of them . Imaging studies find smokers carry roughly 26–36% more of these receptors in the cortex and about 27% more in the striatum than non-smokers. That's why the first cigarette of the day lands so hard and why the tenth barely registers. PET work found that one or two puffs occupies half of those receptors for about three hours, and a whole cigarette occupies 88% . Smoking to satiety hits 95%. A daily smoker keeps them saturated essentially all day, so withdrawal is what happens every time the level drops, many times a day. The good news is that this reverses, and it has been measured in living human brains. Receptor levels stay elevated through about a month of abstinence and return to non-smoker levels by six to twelve weeks . An earlier, smaller study put it closer to three weeks. Either way it's a matter of weeks rather than years, and it's a physical repair, measured directly. One caveat Recovery isn't uniform. The occipital cortex was the last region still measurably elevated at four weeks in the best-designed study, and cerebellar levels at that point tracked with how strongly people were still craving. Feeling fine on paper and still getting hit by urges at week five is normal. It isn't a relapse warning. Every kind of nicotine Built for every product Most quit apps were built for smoking and bolt everything else on afterwards. This one starts from what you use. Cigarettes Peak nicotine within about three minutes of finishing one Vapes & e-cigs Lower peak than a cigarette, but high-strength liquid gets close Pouches A comparable peak, delivered far more slowly, over roughly an hour Dip & chew Slow release, long contact, heavy total daily load Cigars Tracked by count and session rather than pack maths Nicotine gum Counts too, if it's become the habit rather than the exit Hour by hour, then week by week What the timeline looks like The research puts real numbers on this, and they're more encouraging than the folklore. 0–8 HOURS Nicotine's half-life is about two hours. Blood levels peak as you finish and fall fast, and meaningful levels are gone within six to eight hours. Cravings can start about 30 minutes after the last one. DAY 1–2 Onset. Irritability, anxiety, restlessness, trouble concentrating, appetite up, sleep disrupted. Worth knowing: DSM-5 requires four of seven symptoms within 24 hours, and craving is not one of them, which surprises most people. DAY 2–3 The peak. This is when urges are strongest and mood is worst. If you are going to feel like a different person, it's now. FIRST 8 DAYS The window that decides it. Most relapse among people quitting unaided happens inside these eight days. A rough stretch here doesn't mean you're doing it wrong. It means this is the part to plan support around, rather than relying on willpower. WEEK 2–4 It resolves. Total withdrawal score is back at or near pre-quit levels by about two weeks, and essentially there by three or four. Sleep fragmentation clears in five to fourteen days. Anger and impatience are the stubborn ones. WEEK 6–12 Receptors reach non-smoker levels. This is the physical finish line, measured by brain imaging rather than inferred. 6–12 MONTHS Urges fade on an exponential curve. At six months about 13% of people still report strong urges; by twelve months essentially nobody does, though around a third still get occasional ones. Occasional urges aren't failure. Practical What the trials support Backed by evidence Pick a quit day and stop outright. In a 697-person randomised trial, abrupt quitting beat cutting down: 49% vs 39% abstinent at four weeks, 22% vs 16% at six months. Use nicotine replacement or medication. High-certainty evidence: NRT raises quit rates by about half again; varenicline roughly doubles them. If you do cut down first, medicate during the reduction. docs.s: What nicotine did to your brain, and what undoes it
docs.x: The mechanism Nicotine binds nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (chiefly the α4β2 subtype) and leaves them desensitised. Your brain compensates by building more of them . Imaging studies find smokers carry roughly 26–36% more of these receptors in the cortex and about 27% more in the striatum than non-smokers. That's why the first cigarette of the day lands so hard and why the tenth barely registers. PET work found that one or two puffs occupies half of those receptors for about three hours, and a whole cigarette occupies 88% . Smoking to satiety hits 95%. A daily smoker keeps them saturated essentially all day, so withdrawal is what happens every time the level drops, many times a day. The good news is that this reverses, and it has been measured in living human brains. Receptor levels stay elevated through about a month of abstinence and return to non-smoker levels by six to twelve weeks . An earlier, smaller study put it closer to three weeks. Either way it's a matter of weeks rather than years, and it's a physical repair, measured directly. One caveat Recovery isn't uniform. The occipital cortex was the last region still measurably elevated at four weeks in the best-designed study, and cerebellar levels at that point tracked with how strongly people were still craving. Feeling fine on paper and still getting hit by urges at week five is normal. It isn't a relapse warning.

docs.t: CK3 mods not working? Load order, patches and error logs
docs.x: Crusader Kings III When CK3 mods break Load order, checksums, error logs, and how to find the one mod out of forty that is ruining your campaign. Written from years of getting this wrong. Start here The short version Most broken CK3 setups come down to one of four things, and they are worth ruling out in this order before you do anything more involved. One: load order. Two mods changing the same file, in the wrong order. Two: a game patch. CK3 updated, your mods did not. Three: a leftover. An old version of a mod still sitting in your mod folder, still being read. Four: the descriptor. A hand-installed mod whose .mod file points at the wrong place. The rest of this page is each of those in detail, plus how to read the error log and how to find a bad mod without uninstalling everything. If you are installing one of my mods by hand, the step-by-step lives on the download pages instead: The Long Night and Supernatural . Where things live The three folders that matter Mods you installed by hand, and the .mod files that describe them, live in your CK3 user directory: Windows Documents\Paradox Interactive\Crusader Kings III\mod\ macOS ~/Documents/Paradox Interactive/Crusader Kings III/mod/ Linux ~/.local/share/Paradox Interactive/Crusader Kings III/mod/ Mods you subscribed to on the Steam Workshop do not go there. They land in Steam's own folder, under CK3's app id: Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\1158310\ Each subfolder in there is named after the Workshop item's id, which is the long number at the end of its Workshop URL. That is how you work out which downloaded folder is which mod. The third folder is the one almost nobody opens, and it is where the answers are: Documents\Paradox Interactive\Crusader Kings III\logs\ The launcher never mentions it. It holds error.log , and more on that further down. The one rule Lower wins This is the single most useful thing to understand about CK3 mods, and it is one sentence. When two mods contain the same file, the one lower in the playset overwrites the one above it . That is the whole mechanic. The load order is not a suggestion or a loading sequence; it is a stack of overwrites, resolved top to bottom, file by file. Two consequences follow, and between them they explain most "why is this mod not doing anything" reports. The first: a mod that seems to have no effect is usually not broken. It is being overwritten by something below it that touches the same files. Move it down. The second, which catches people out more: sorting a mod below another one is not the same as disabling it. If two mods ship the same file and you push one to the bottom, the one at the bottom wins that file — but every file the loser has that the winner does not is still loaded. You end up with a mix of both. When two mods are genuinely incompatible, the fix is to untick one, not to reorder it. Compatibility patches exist because of this rule. A patch is a mod that contains the merged version of the files two other mods both changed, which is why a patch always goes last: it has to be the one doing the final overwrite. After an update The patch that broke everything CK3 updates. Your mods do not update at the same moment, because a human has to go and fix each one. This is the most common cause of a save that will not load and a main menu full of red. What actually happens: a mod replaces whole files. When Paradox changes one of those files in a patch, the mod is still handing the game its older copy, which now refers to things that moved or no longer exist. The mod is not corrupt. It is out of date, which looks identical from the outside. The supported_version line in a mod's descriptor is the author saying which game version they last checked it against. The launcher shows a warning when that does not match your game. Take the warning seriously but not literally — plenty of mods keep working across a patch that changed nothing they touch, and an author who has not updated the line yet is common. It is a hint, not a verdict. If a patch just landed and everything is on fire, the honest answer is usually to wait a few days. Big mods get fixed. Starting a fresh campaign on a broken setup is how you lose thirty hours of it later. Finding the culprit Halve it, do not hunt it With forty mods enabled and a crash on load, the instinct is to guess which one it is. Do not guess. Halving finds it in about five or six launches no matter how many mods you have, and guessing can take all evening. Turn off the bottom half of your playset. Launch. If it works, the problem is in the half you turned off; if it still breaks, it is in the half you kept. Either way you have just eliminated half your list. Take the half that contains the problem, cut that in half, and go again. Forty mods becomes twenty, ten, five, three, two, one. Two things make this go wrong. Keep any mod that others depend on switched on the whole time — for a Game of Thrones setup that means AGOT itself, since every submod fails without it and you will get a false result on every round. And change one thing per launch. Toggling a mod and reordering another in the same pass means you no longer know which one did it. When you are down to a single mod, check its Workshop comments or its Discord before reporting anything. Whatever you found, someone found it four days ago. error.log Reading the log without being a programmer Open Documents\Paradox Interactive\Crusader Kings III\logs\error.log in any text editor. It is plain text and it is written fresh each time the game runs, so the quickest thing you can do is delete it, launch, reproduce the problem, and read what is in the new one. Now everything in the file belongs to the run that just failed. It will be long, and most of it does not matter. Vanilla CK3 logs errors about itself on a completely clean install, so a file with a few hundred lines is not evidence of anything. You are not trying to get it to zero. What you are looking for is a filename you recognise and a reason next to it. Lines naming a specific file in a specific mod are worth reading. Lines about a missing localization key are usually cosmetic — that is the cause of text showing up as a raw key like my_trait_desc instead of a sentence. Lines about a trait, event or decision that could not be found are the ones that break behaviour, and they usually mean a mod is referring to something another mod removed or renamed. You do not have to diagnose it. Finding the mod name in the log and pasting the line into that mod's Discord is enough, and it is dramatically more useful to the author than "it crashes". Worth correcting Mods and achievements: the advice you have read is out of date The received wisdom is that mods disable achievements and that you need Ironman for them. That was true once and it is worth knowing it changed, because a lot of guides still say it. Since CK3 version 1.9, neither Ironman mode nor an unmodified checksum is required for achievements to stay enabled . A modded game can still earn them. What does still switch them off is certain game rules — broadly the ones that make the game easier. That is a per-rule thing rather than a mod thing, and the game tells you when a rule you have picked will do it. So if achievements are the reason you have been playing unmodded, that reason has expired. Rolling back Staying on an older version on purpose Sometimes the right answer is to not take the patch. A campaign you are forty years into, on a mod list that works, is worth more than the newest version number. Steam keeps older CK3 builds available as beta branches. In your Steam library, right-click Crusader Kings III, open Properties, and look under Betas — the previous major versions are listed there, and picking one downloads that build. The mods you already have keep working because the game stopped moving. Two warnings. Saves made on a newer version will generally not open on an older one, so roll back before you play rather than after. And multiplayer requires everyone on the same version, so agree it with whoever you play with first. There is no equivalent on Game Pass, and GOG and Epic handle old builds differently. If you are not on Steam, keeping your own copy of a mod version that works is the closest thing to insurance you have. Habits Four things that save the evening Keep a playset you do not touch. Make a second playset with the handful of mods you know work together and leave it alone. When something breaks, launching that one tells you in thirty seconds whether the problem is a mod or the game itself. Delete old versions properly. Unsubscribing on the Workshop usually removes the files; a hand-installed mod never does. Both the folder and its .mod file have to go, and a leftover .mod file pointing at a folder that is gone is its own flavour of confusing. Add mods one at a time when a campaign is running. Mid-save changes are not automatically dangerous, but six at once means you cannot tell which one caused the thing you noticed

docs.x: Community Four servers, one host I've been building Discord communities since Discord was the new kid. Pick the room that fits. The Game Center Est. May 2016, the original Started in May 2016 as a Skype replacement for my friend group. I'd found Discord before most people had heard of it and made us a server with a plain controller icon. It was never meant to be a "community project"; it kept growing into one anyway. Holiday merch giveaways, game nights, years of running jokes, and eventually its own website. The icon has changed with every season, and the same people are still talking to each other. Join The Game Center Read the full story → Dlonem's Den Est. 2019, the home base The server that goes with the YouTube channel. Video drops, behind-the-scenes on the apps, and whatever I'm currently obsessed with. If you found me through a video, this is your room. Join the Den The Long Night & Azor Ahai Est. 2026, the newest The server for the Long Night & Azor Ahai mod for A Game of Thrones. Patch notes go up here first, bug reports get answered, and load-order questions get sorted out before they ruin anyone's campaign. It's the newest of the four and it's filling fast. Join the Long Night server Supernatural For the mod The official server for the Crusader Kings III Supernatural mod. Report bugs, pitch ideas, ask questions, and have a say in where the mod goes next. Player input has driven a lot of what's in it already. Join the Supernatural server Four doors Which one you actually want Four servers sounds like more than it is. They are not four versions of the same room, and joining all of them is usually the wrong move. If you play one of the mods and something is broken , go straight to that mod's server — The Long Night or Supernatural . That is where patch notes land first and where load-order problems get sorted out, usually by another player before I have even seen the message. It is the fastest help available anywhere, including email. If you found me through a video , the Den is the one. It is the server attached to the YouTube channel: uploads, what I am building, and whatever I am currently obsessed with. If you just want somewhere to hang out , The Game Center is the oldest room and the least on-topic one. It has been running since 2016 and it is mostly people who have known each other for years talking nonsense. The whole story is here if you want it. If your problem is with an app , Discord is the slowest route. Use the support page instead — app problems need details like your device and version that are easier to send by email. Before you knock How these rooms are run I have been moderating Discord servers since 2016 and I have landed on a fairly boring philosophy about it, which I think is the correct one. Bug reports are welcome and blunt ones are the most useful. "It crashes when I press the button" is worth more than a polite paragraph that avoids saying what broke. If you are annoyed at something I made, say so — I would rather hear it than have you leave quietly. Nobody has to be interesting to belong there. I wrote messages years ago for people who join a server and then never speak, because sitting in a room where everyone already knows each other is genuinely hard and that should not be the thing that stops you. Lurking indefinitely is a completely acceptable way to use all four of these. What I do not run is a hype server. There is no engagement bot, no levelling system, and nothing that pings everyone. If I have shipped something you will see it once.

docs.t: Legacy — how Dlonem became Dlonem
docs.x: The legacy One made-up word, earned slowly Nobody sets out to be called Dlonem. It took a random name generator, a decade as a potato, and one rebrand to get here. Watch the moon fill in. 2008 – 2010 · ROBLOX Carlman622 Every online life starts with a first username you can't explain. Mine was Carlman622, on Roblox. The account is still out there, frozen in a striped hoodie and a Roblox cap it's been wearing since January 2010. Nobody, me included, has ever worked out what the name was supposed to mean. The dream project back then was an authentic Hunger Games map. This was before Discord, and before Skype was a given, so my cousin Randy and I would fire up Roblox and call each other on our families' landlines , staying on for hours while we played. Unlimited phone plans had not reached either of our houses yet. Randy's mom eventually opened a phone bill with hours upon hours of our calls itemized on it, easily a couple hundred dollars' worth. The Hunger Games map was never finished. The bill is the real legacy. 2009 – 2011 · WRATH OF THE LICH KING Noaha the Warlock Middle school, World of Warcraft. A warlock named Noaha carried me through the Lich King era, including a proud stretch of joining Icecrown Citadel raids I had no business being in. I'd get kicked for having no idea what I was doing, queue back up, and try again. I never made it past the second boss. Damn, I would try. ~2010 · THE GENERATOR A death knight needs a name Sixth grade, going on seventh. It was time to roll a death knight, and I couldn't think of a name, so I hit WoW's random name generator over and over, never quite liking any of it. Then I took one result, removed a couple letters, swapped another, and landed on a word that didn't exist anywhere: Dlonem . I named the character and moved on. It would be sixteen years before the word had a real job. 2011 – 2017 · STEAM The Mr.Potato years On Steam I became Mr.Potato, and to basically everyone who knew me, just Potato . (One guy insisted on "Tater." There's always one.) Old friends from that era still call me Potato today, so I would say it stuck. Right up to the rebrand, my profile picture wasn't even a potato. For a while it was a turtle in a baseball cap. I didn't have my own thing going yet, and getting one is what everything after this is about. the pre-brand aesthetic, preserved MAY 2016 · DISCORD The Game Center Back then the friend group lived on Skype, because it was simpler than Steam voice: always on, and you could call anybody. Then I stumbled onto Discord before most people had heard of it, and moved us over. It started as a group server with a plain little game controller for an icon. There was no "TGC" and no grand plan, just "wouldn't it be cool to meet more people to game with?" It blew up into something bigger anyway: holiday merch giveaways, game nights every couple months, seasonal icons for every holiday, and me playing the designated adult in a server full of teenagers. ("You probably shouldn't be saying that" was the moderation policy.) It even got its own website. Ten years later the server still exists, and so do all forty-something versions of that controller icon. TGC, est. may 2016 LATE 2019 · THE REBRAND The word comes back A potato is hard to build a brand on. Looking for a name that was mine , I remembered the death knight. Dlonem was unique, unclaimed everywhere, and already had history. The YouTube channel launched under it in 2019, and the letter D started showing up in profile pictures, first in a ghostly Danny Phantom style, later sharpened into the crescent-and-scythe mark it is now. the danny phantom era, july 2019 JULY 1, 2026 · NOW Dlonem LLC Today the word covers a YouTube channel, four Discord communities, two Crusader Kings III mods with thousands of subscribers, and a small studio shipping privacy-friendly mobile apps, officially incorporated as Dlonem LLC on July 1, 2026. Six lifestyles with ten perk trees, supernatural regiments, artifacts, twenty-one game rules, and since 2.35 a hunt where every monster is a real character who left a trail. You can play the hunter, or rule as something far older. 11,200+ subscribers 51,000+ visitors 1,800+ favorites Read the full breakdown Steam Workshop Non-Steam download Discord Running both at once The compatibility patch This is for running vampires and the army of the dead in the same campaign. Both mods rewrite some of the same files, and whichever loads second erases the other's version without warning. The patch fixes that. AGOT: Supernatural & The Long Night Compatibility Patch needs all three mods It does nothing on its own, and it has to load last. Twenty-two entries that both mods define. Each one is a three-way merge against the base game's own version, so neither mod's changes are guessed at. Marriage acceptance. AGOT's full 1,000-line house and legitimacy logic, plus Supernatural's fertility exemptions. Without the patch one of the two is gone; this entry alone was behind multiplayer desyncs in testing. Births. AGOT's entire birth pipeline (house looks, Valyrian genetics, dragon dreams) and Supernatural's, in one file. Both ship it at the same path, so the later one was deleting the other wholesale. The Originals. Supernatural's founding vampire family is written for the vanilla map, with a Norse culture and faith that don't exist in Westeros. Under the patch they become First Men of the North: northman culture, Old Gods faith. Plus disinheritance, the witch ritual, secrets, schemes, abductions, artifact demands, traits, imprisonment and resurrection rules. 1,367 running it right now 22 merged entries v1.0 current release Load order: drag the patch to the very bottom A Game of Thrones AGOT submods (AGOT+, Valyrian Steel, Submod Core, Nobility…) AGOT: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Supernatural The Compatibility Patch (this one, last) Every fix works by defining the entry the two mods fight over. Anything loaded after it wins instead, and the patch does nothing at all. View on Steam Workshop New to this If you have never installed a CK3 mod On Steam it is genuinely one click. Open the Workshop page, hit Subscribe, and the next time you open the Paradox launcher the mod is in your list waiting to be added to a playset. Nothing to unzip and nothing to configure. Off Steam — GOG, Epic, Game Pass — it is about five minutes of copying a folder and writing one small text file by hand. Both of my mods have a page that walks the whole thing: The Long Night and Supernatural . The part that trips up almost everyone is not installing a mod. It is the load order. CK3 resolves conflicts by letting the mod lower in your playset overwrite the one above it, which means a mod that appears to do nothing is usually being overwritten rather than being broken, and sorting two incompatible mods rather than disabling one of them leaves you running a mixture of both. I wrote up the whole thing — load order, what a game patch does to a mod, finding the one bad mod out of forty, and how to read the error log — on a separate page: when CK3 mods break . It applies to any mod, not just mine. Running both Why there is a third thing in the list The compatibility patch confuses people until the load-order rule explains it, and then it is obvious. Supernatural and The Long Night both change some of the same underlying files. Loaded together without anything else, whichever one sits lower wins those files outright and the other one quietly loses whatever it had put there. Neither mod is at fault; that is just what overwriting means. The patch is a small third mod that contains the merged version of exactly those files — the pieces of both, reconciled. It has to load last , because its entire job is to be the final overwrite. Put it anywhere else and something else overwrites the merge, which puts you back where you started. You only need it if you are running both mods in the same campaign. One mod on its own does not need a patch for anything.

docs.t: Download Supernatural — CK3 mod without Steam
docs.x: Manual install Download without Steam Supernatural is plain files, so it runs on any copy of Crusader Kings III: GOG, Epic, Game Pass, wherever you bought it. It takes about ten minutes by hand, and this page walks the whole thing. Home › Mods › Supernatural › Download If your CK3 is on Steam, use the Workshop instead It's one click, it keeps itself current, and it handles the load order for you. Nothing on this page is better; it exists for people who can't use the Workshop at all. Subscribe on the Steam Workshop → Step zero Get the files The mod is open source. The repository is the download, with no mirror, no shortener and no waiting. Download from GitHub Browse the source current release on GitHub CK3 1.19.0.6 no other mods required free, forever On the newest release, take Source code (zip) under Assets. The .tar.gz is the same files in a wrapper Windows can't open on its own, so stick with the zip. Fair warning about the size. Supernatural is a large mod. The art alone is a few hundred megabytes, so expect a download in that range rather than a quick one. That is the mod itself, not padding, and it is the same weight the Workshop copy takes up on your disk. Ten minutes Installing it by hand Unzip it The archive holds one folder named after the version, something like CK3SupernaturalMod-2.35 . Open it. That outer folder is only packaging and is not what goes into your game. Inside are the two things you need, sitting side by side: supernatural_mod : the mod folder, containing common , events , gfx , gui , history , localization , music and descriptor.mod supernatural_mod.mod : a small text file the launcher reads You need both . A handful of .txt changelogs and .py helper scripts sit inside the mod folder as well. They're leftovers from building it; the game ignores them, and you can leave them exactly where they are. Move both into your CK3 mod directory The folder and the .mod file go here together, and the .mod file sits next to the folder, never inside it: Windows Documents\Paradox Interactive\Crusader Kings III\mod\ macOS ~/Documents/Paradox Interactive/Crusader Kings III/mod/ Linux ~/.local/share/Paradox Interactive/Crusader Kings III/mod/ If there's no mod folder there yet, launch CK3 once and close it, or create the folder yourself. Replace the .mod file (don't skip this one) This is the step that decides whether any of the rest works, and it is not optional . The supernatural_mod.mod file inside the download was written on my computer, and it still carries the folder path from my computer. On your machine that path doesn't exist, so the launcher reports a descriptor error and the mod never shows up. docs.s: The invasion is a four-phase struggle
docs.x: The struggle Each phase changes what your counties produce and how close the dead are. Dead dragons, lost rangings and a hollowed-out Watch all move the tracker, so you can plan your preparations against something you can see. THE LONG SUMMER Peace, a +5% county modifier , and a counter you can see from day one. This is the window you get to spend. WINTER IS COMING −5% county modifier. Length is unknown, and your own losses shorten it. THE LONG NIGHT The invasion, at a −10% county modifier . Dragonglass in the cellars and men sent north is the whole difference between surviving it and being surprised by it. THE DAWN A ruined North to rebuild, and one crown-level choice that outlasts the war. The same tracker in the Long Summer, Winter Is Coming and the Long Night. The catalyst list underneath is what moved it. A quiet century still ends on schedule. A bad one ends early.

docs.s: Azor Ahai has a whole system behind it
docs.x: The prophecy There is no Azor Ahai trait to tick in the ruler designer. Every character in the world is measured against the prophecy continuously, their standing moves as marks are earned and lost, and the AI is competing for it too. Nine marks, and you never need all nine Dragon dreams, and greensight Born in salt and smoke, or beneath a bleeding star Hidden blood: a Valyrian bastard raised inside a great house Walking among the dead and surviving it Carrying spellforged steel Waking dragons from stone Dying, and not staying dead Five are decided at birth and four are earned. Two of them are checked continuously: lose the sword or the dragon and the claim goes with it. Read the Signs tells you which you carry, and costs nothing. And the realm decides what it means Deeds need validating by a red priest, a witch or a greenseer, since an unwitnessed miracle counts for nothing Two deeds make you Favored of R'hllor ; four make you Chosen (a game rule can make it one and three, or three and six) Lightbringer can be forged, at the price every version of the tale agrees on The man who ends it is called the Prince That Was Promised , the Dawnbringer if he did it with a Lightbringer he forged, or, failing both, the Dawn Kill the Night King and you are Azor Ahai Reborn , marks or no marks The AI plays all of it; rival claimants meet, and sometimes ally Lightbringer, once it is finally out of the third quench. Whether the one they named was ever the prince is decided behind the curtain, and the world only finds out at the end. There are four ways that can land.

The complete notes for every release, with reporter credits, are on the Workshop change-notes page and in the GitHub wiki . 1.1.1 — The Watch Keeps No Land A sworn brother renounces any land he inherits outside the Wall, the Lord Commander included; the exemption was how the Watch ended up holding a random county in the North. The dead answer to nobody living. Stannis gets Melisandre when he sends for a priest, and the lord of Dragonstone usually does. The Others cannot run schemes. Every county the dead take is set to full control so their own peasants never rise against them, and their land recovers control after a siege instead of never, which also stops the invasion stalling on its own revolts. The Crown of the Others no longer refuses its own king, and a load error on the house of the Others is gone. 1.1.0b — Keeping pace with A Game of Thrones A hotfix for AGOT's 0.5.2 hotfix. An invasion war counts its goal as held once the dead occupy six tenths of it, so held ground plus a won field closes a war inside a season instead of a second winter. The seventy-two named dragons look the way AGOT now paints them, a camp with a dragon in it cannot be moved beyond an intact Wall, and dragon eggs are held by the right people. 1.1.0a — One Host A hotfix, no new content. The dead stop fighting the dead: the Others no longer declare de jure wars, a war with the dead on both sides cannot be declared on thirteen casus belli, and the Night King's own invasion can no longer be aimed at his own. Nobody keeps an alliance with the dead, and the living no longer serve them. From a full playthrough log: the Trial of Seven no longer carves one name three times, the spear card shows its portraits, and the two cards that could land on the same day no longer contradict each other. Twelve fixes. 1.1.0 — The Last Hour The Night King is fought on foot, in the snow, by you and the people who were there with you. Lose and he keeps you. White Walkers can be met during Winter Is Coming. The character page records the war. A rider can force a dragon over a standing Wall. The Wall's fall is told to everyone in their own station. His host grows with his conquest, from twenty thousand beyond the Wall to two hundred thousand once the North falls, and a field kill no longer ends the Long Night; only a bane does. Underneath it, the largest fix pass the mod has had, including three overrides that had never run at all. 1.0.16a — The Wanderer The Night King keeps his land on older saves, answers to nobody, and can pay his men again. docs.x: Full disclosure You deserve to know what a submod touches, so here is the whole list. Every entry is a same-name override of exactly one AGOT definition: their body copied in full, one documented change, re-checked against their current version every release. It is longer than it used to be, because the mod is. Nineteen definitions Six scripted rules : alliances (nothing living keeps an alliance with the dead), who may be played (a character raised as one of the dead hands off to an heir), the second chance at a natural death (the red priest's last kiss), who may be a guest, who may be regent (never a sworn brother, never for a wight), and who may move a camp (ranging captains, like the First Ranger) Eight scripted triggers : knights, court positions, councillors and commanders (the living do not serve the dead, and the Night King may lead his own host), capture (he is imprisoned rather than randomly slain in a siege), regency for personal reasons, who may become a landless adventurer (never one of the dead), and one check thirteen AGOT casus belli share (the dead cannot declare war on the dead) Three scripted effects : how rulers are named (wights, ranging captains and wardens get their titles; every other mod's titles pass straight through), what happens when a dragon dies in a dragon duel (the dead may claim it), and the melee's scene (snow, not a tourney ground) One decision, one casus belli : Restore the Night's Watch (refounded only when there is no Watch left), and the independence war (a sworn brother cannot secede from the Lord Commander) And two that merge rather than replace The ranger-camp domicile, so a ranging captain can hold a camp at all, and the Night's Watch title-gain handler, so appointing one doesn't force a government change on him. Everything else sits alongside AGOT rather than on top of it. The mod is safe to add and to update mid-save, though game rules are baked in when a save is created, so an existing campaign keeps whatever rules it started with. Built on the work of others. This is a fork standing on Freeholder's original Long Night, Tehaen's 1.19 update, and Wepo94's The Long Night+.

docs.x: For the ones who read this far It has no handle on the outside. It opens for one kind of lord, it is checked exactly once — at the moment your character first draws breath — and nobody has ever stumbled into it by accident. The riddle of the household ledger Three decisions sit behind it. They do not appear greyed out with their requirements listed; if you are not the one it is waiting for, they do not exist . That is how it was built. Everything you need is below. Nothing below is a lie. Found your own house — and answer to no one above you. Take the sin the septons put in the flesh, and the virtue they put in the work. Both. They sit oddly together. That is rather the point. Then set your sword-arm at three fives — not one more, and not one less. Do all of it in the ruler designer, before the first snow. docs.x: Common questions Do I really have to disable the other Long Night mods? Yes, and it's the single most common cause of something being broken. This mod is a fork of both AGOT: The Long Night and The Long Night+, and it ships files at the same paths. Load order won't save you: either of them enabled anywhere in your playset overrides this mod with older code. They have to be disabled, not sorted lower. You can unsubscribe from them entirely. Do I need to start a new game? No. It's safe to add and to update mid-save. The one caveat is that CK3 bakes game rules in when a save is created, so an existing campaign keeps whatever rules it started with. If you want to change the invasion timing or difficulty, that needs a fresh save. Does it work with Supernatural? Yes, with the compatibility patch. Load this mod, then Supernatural, then AGOT: Supernatural & The Long Night Compatibility Patch last. Supernatural has its own page here if you haven't seen it. What if I use other dragon mods? Pick them at campaign start and keep them. Dead dragons' appearances are stored against the exact set of portrait genes loaded at the time, so adding or removing any gene-adding mod mid-save can scramble dragons that have already died. Living dragons are unaffected. What version of CK3 is it for? CK3 1.19.0.6, built against the current release of A Game of Thrones. How do I actually kill the Night King? Beat the dead in the field once; that opens the War for the Dawn, which only an independent ruler can declare. Reach him, and the confrontation is the Last Hour: a Trial-of-Seven melee, you and your companions against him and his Walkers. Bring a bane. Dragonglass, Valyrian steel, Lightbringer or dragonfire destroy him; anything else casts him down and the dark crowns another. The Russian translation covers most of the mod; the newest events (the Last Hour, the encounter, the spear, consecration, travel danger) are still in English. The Steam Workshop comments work too.

docs.s: The Night King and his host
docs.x: The Night King He is created at the Frigid Rise on the day the invasion opens: six to eight thousand years old, martial 25, intrigue 100, learning 65, prowess 30, carrying the traits Other and Great Other, and the nickname the Night King . His culture is the Others (frostborn in the files), his faith the Cold Gods, his house the Others, his realm The Land of Always Winter , renamed The Long Night once he holds thirty counties. He takes the hegemony and fifteen counties beyond the Wall on day one, is made independent, and receives the Crown of the Others and the Crystal Sword. He leads his host in person. Every Night King who follows inherits the same kit, so killing one with ordinary steel does not leave the dead weaker. His culture cannot be reasoned with: the dead learn nothing (their innovations are Bronze Age and never advance), keep no mercenaries, buy nothing, and have every county opinion at +400 so nothing of theirs ever revolts. The Night King's court is sixty-two elite Others, and every ten days it is re-sacrificed: frostborn courtiers are made Others, everyone else and every prisoner dies. Since 1.1.1 the Others, the Night King and wights cannot run hostile or personal schemes at all. How big his host is Two forces. The elite host is fixed: ten thousand of The Dead (damage 38, toughness 75, siege tier 4) plus trebuchets, needing no supply. The Risen Dead horde (damage 3, toughness 25, counters peasant militia, costs him nothing to keep) is a milestone top-up, refilled every thirty days up to four regiments at a time: Milestone Standard target Weak ×0.75 Strong ×1.25 Insane ×1.5 The invasion opens 20,000 15,000 25,000 30,000 Everything beyond the Wall is his 50,000 37,500 62,500 75,000 Castle Black has fallen 100,000 75,000 125,000 150,000 The North is done 200,000 150,000 250,000 300,000 140 counties or more 250,000 187,500 312,500 375,000 The hard cap is 500,000, the population of King's Landing. Both units fight better in winter. His commanders carry The Dead Do Not Tire , which halves siege morale loss and shortens siege phases by a quarter. Under The Cycle later waves stack more on top (see After the Dawn ). docs.x: The Wall comes down when the dead take Castle Black: the Watch is at war with the Night King and he holds the county, or Castle Black is already in dead hands. Every player gets the cinematic The Wall Has Fallen , and the middle section of the Wall breaks on the map. A fifth of every black brother flees south; sworn brothers who held castles keep them, and the rest are pooled at Winterfell, Karhold and the Last Hearth. Castle Black takes The Wall Is Broken (−15 county opinion, −20% development growth, −15% supply). Thirty days later comes The Age of Heroes Is Ended , opening in your own station: sworn brother, free folk, blood of the dragon, northman, red priest, lord, or nobody. It writes the memory alive when the Wall fell . Thirty days after that Castle Black is ruined, the North stage of the invasion opens, and the horde's next milestone unlocks. The moment the dead hold any county on the Wall, the ward is gone: living dragons can fight beyond the Wall without the penalty, and the +60 the spear gets against a dragon forced over an intact Wall is removed. If the living retake the Wall, the ward returns. Under The Cycle , the Wall is raised again in the next Long Summer. Once the Long Night arrives, Black Cloaks at Your Gates can reach dukes and up across the Seven Kingdoms (never Dorne, the Reach or the Stormlands): real survivors from the Wall first, one stranger if the list is empty. Take them in and up to three join you, followed by What the Watch Left You , which can put Black Cloaks on the Walls on your realm for twenty years (+5% garrison, +5% reinforcement, +2 advantage).

docs.x: Who gets raised Dying is not the trigger; being taken into the dead's realm is . Anyone who gains a title from one of the dead, any vassal they gain, every courtier of an Other, and every living person in the Night King's service is converted, along with their court. Before it happens a landless noble may flee (a base 15% chance, more if craven, less if brave), and a landed lord may flee south as a refugee of the Dawn (base 10%), which is also the Flee South decision offered to any lord the dark is coming for. A wight keeps his face, his titles and his realm, now under the Risen Thrall government, which is unplayable by design: a player who is raised hands off to an heir. The trait Wight makes him tireless (health +50, immortal, incapacitated, cannot marry or have children, no inheritance), hated (−150 general opinion) and dreaded (+25). Every alliance, friendship, love and marriage he had is severed, and his spouse gets Death Did Us Part . Close family, friends and lovers who are players get A Face I Know when someone they knew rises. A wight is never promoted to an Other. The Night King's own kill is different. Lose the Last Hour to him and you are raised as an Other , not a wight, with the Other trait, the house of the Others and the flag that puts you on his side of the line the next time a champion reaches him. A landed champion stays landed in the dead's host. When the Night King is destroyed, every wight and every risen dragon dies where it stands, every living member of the house of the Others is gone save one (see the Cycle ), and the land the dead held is scoured. Undead dragons Under the default rule, They Raise Their Kills , the Others are given nothing. A dragon that dies during the Long Night with the dead involved, killed by one of them or dying over ground they hold, is recorded, and every three years, if the Night King has no dragon, one recorded dragon is raised: same name, same face, same size, the colour of ice, immortal, carrying the trait Risen and the nickname the Undead . Further dragons go to his lieutenants. A dragon that dies fighting another dragon over ground the dead can claim is not killed but taken in place , and its rider gets The Wrong Colour . An undead dragon that dies stays dead. One Simply Appears hands him a dragon while dragons exist anywhere; Off means never. The spear In any Long Night battle where the Night King commands or fights, if the dead have no dragon and the spear is not on cooldown, one rider on the field is drawn at random and he throws. The three-year cooldown arms on the throw, hit or miss. docs.x: The Watch's realm is renamed The Night's Watch . Nineteen castles on the Wall, eight ranging companies with camps on the map, a Lord Commander with decisions nobody else gets, and a set of rules that keep the Watch out of southern politics whether it likes it or not. Taking the black The decision is Take the Black . It is open to any adult man standing in the Seven Kingdoms who is not free folk, not a maester or septon, not already a sworn brother and not one of the dead, while a Lord Commander exists and a ranging company is free (vacant, or held by an AI captain he can stand down). You need somewhere for the realm to go: an heir, a liege, or nothing to give up. There is no prestige requirement. Women are refused at the gate. What it costs is the oath: every title you hold passes to your primary heir, or to your liege if you have none, with no claim kept; your marriage, betrothal, claims, debts, Iron Bank shares and Kingsguard place end at the Wall; any dragon that answers to you is unbonded; any adventurer company you led is disbanded. Your successor remembers it (+40 opinion for sixty years), your family and former vassals think better of you for it, and your close family moves to the heir's court. What you get is a ranging company of your own, sworn to the Lord Commander, and you play on as the brother. The eight ranging companies The companies are The Long Ranging, The Deep Ranging, The Cold Ranging, The Silent Ranging, The Black Ranging, The Winter Ranging, The Far Ranging and The Last Ranging . Each is a landless title under the Wall with a real camp on the map, a captain titled Ranger-Captain , and its own government, Ranging Company : army upkeep −60%, men-at-arms upkeep −70%, +2 martial and +2 prowess per prestige level, +0.5 monthly dread, and no holy orders. The camp is the ranger camp AGOT gives the First Ranger, opened to all eight companies, and it can only be pitched on the Wall or beyond it, never with raised armies. From game start each company has a historical northman captain, and a new captain every generation, all the way to 8320. A captain can March the Ranging to Craster's Keep, Whitetree or Hardhome and Return to the Wall ; the camp travels, provisions are topped up at the Wall, and the arrival is quiet by design. Once a year, if the Lord Commander's court holds ten or more brothers who could be posted, each company with fewer than six ranging brothers gets one, weighted toward rangers, the brave and the strong. Captains compete for First Ranger : when the holder dies, an AI captain is chosen (martial and prowess of 12 or more, the ranger lifestyle and bravery all count) and moves to that seat; player captains are not drafted into it. Under the default rule the Watch fills companies one through five itself and holds three open for players; Leave Them for Players leaves a dead captain's seat waiting; All Eight Ride keeps every company manned. When a captain dies, the company passes to a qualifying brother of the Lord Commander's court, or a ranger is created for it, or the Lord Commander holds it himself. A ranger who has been sworn long enough (a hundred points of the Night's Watch trait; a recruit does not get given a castle) can Ask for a Castle and trade the company for a keepership. The Wall's castles Castle Black is the Lord Commander's own seat. The other eighteen castles are keeperships held from him: Deep Lake, Icemark, Greyguard, Stonedoor, Hoarfrost Hill, Queensgate, Oakenshield, Woodswatch-by-the-Pool, Sable Hall, Rimegate, Westwatch-by-the-Bridge, Sentinel Stand, Long Barrow, The Torches, Greenguard, and the three county seats, the Nightfort, the Shadow Tower and Eastwatch-by-the-Sea, which are granted last because each carries several baronies with it. docs.x: A red priest can spend himself on one person, once, ever. There are two roads back and both need the priest in place before you die. What you must do beforehand Have a red priest. He needs the Red Priest trait, to be an available adult, to have at least a first level of devotion or a learning of 10, and to have never given the last kiss. Get one with Send for a Red Priest , or appoint any R'hllor courtier as court chaplain and AGOT gives him the trait. Take Ask for the Lord's Blessing. It is free, has no cooldown and no faith requirement. It is shown whenever a priest who can bless you is within reach: your court chaplain, a ranging company's camp priest, or any courtier or guest. You cannot take it while imprisoned or while another priest's words already stand over you. The priest can also offer it to you himself ( Offer the Lord's Blessing ); refusing him costs him piety. Either way The Words Are Said . Keep him alive and unspent. If your priest dies, the bond is released and you can ask another. If he spends his one kiss on someone else, he is spent forever and you are free to ask again. Ask again after any change of priest. Give the fire a reason. The priest's answer is not automatic (see below). Being Favored or Chosen, having even one prophecy mark, or fighting in Winter Is Coming or the Long Night makes him far likelier to pay; being his friend makes refusal rare. Falling in battle With the blessing on you, the day you fall in a battle as a knight or a commander you are wounded instead of killed and carry Fell in the Dark (health −1.5, prowess −4). The next day you get You Do Not Get Up . Two days later your priest, wherever he is, gets Send For Me, Whatever Is Left : he pays ( Take it out of me, then. Not him. ) or refuses ( Not this one. R'hllor forgive me, not this one. ). His odds to pay are 70 against 30 to refuse as a base; being worth the fire adds 50 to paying and, if you are not, 60 to refusing; friendship adds 40 to paying and cuts refusal to a fifth. If he pays, a day later you get The Fire Gave You Back , and the Get up button is the resurrection. If he refuses, The Fire Kept What It Had arrives and its only option kills you. You have to survive the three days in between; if your wounds take you first he cannot pay. Whether your death lands in this pool at all is a weighted draw against the game's own battle deaths: base 40 as a knight and 8 as a commander, halved outside the cold, half again more in the Long Night and for a champion of R'hllor. A natural death This road needs no blessing. If you die of age, illness or wounds outside battle, you get a second chance when all of these hold: your faith has the doctrine that lets it heal through the flames, a qualifying red priest sits as your court chaplain (or camp priest), you are under 65 and not infirm, and the fire wants you, meaning you are Favored, Chosen or Azor Ahai Reborn, hold at least one prophecy mark, or are taking part in the struggle during Winter Is Coming or the Long Night. Then The Last Kiss fires the next day. This route costs 150 piety as well. What it costs You come back carrying Returned by R'hllor : +6 martial, +12 prowess, +3 stewardship, +1.5 health, twenty years of life expectancy, −30% stress gain, +25 same-faith opinion, +1 monthly piety, a lower chance of dying in combat, and −35% fertility. Every return adds 25 to the trait's track and takes something with it: the first leaves you scarred, the second takes an eye (or disfigures you), the third takes a leg, a face or a hand, and every one after that maims. At 50 the trait reads Twice-Returned , at 75 Thrice-Returned , at 100 Kept by the Fire ; each rung adds dread and takes health and fertility, and the last two turn the world against you. Reaching him The War for the Dawn can only be declared once the dead have lost a war or the Night King has been cast down in the field, and only by an independent ruler holding a county or more, with a thousand men and a dynasty of some standing; vassals march to their liege's war, and anyone can join one already running. The Iron Throne declares it if it is held, and everyone else joins. It has no white peace, and losing it costs 500 prestige and gives him five years' respite. The decision reads: The War for the Dawn cannot be declared while the Others savor a recent victory. Three roads lead to a scene. Win a battle he is standing in, as commander or knight, and the winning commander gets The Field Afterwards two days later. Win the War for the Dawn on score and the worthiest attacker, or the worthiest knight among them, gets The Last Hour with him on the field. Imprison him and his captor, or the worthiest of the captor's knights and courtiers, gets the same card with him in chains. Worthiness is the prophecy's arithmetic plus prowess, minus wounds, and a man carrying a bane outranks everyone who is not. The Field Afterwards The card reads differently depending on what you brought: Lightbringer, Dawn, a dragon overhead, Valyrian steel, dragonglass, a dragon the dead took from you, nothing at all. The choices: End it. A single duel against him. Shown greyed if you carry nothing that can hurt him. Winning is a roll weighted by what you carry (Lightbringer +60, Dawn +55, Valyrian steel +35, dragonglass +20), what you are (Chosen +30, Azor Ahai Reborn +25, Favored +15, Returned +10, brave +10), what you have survived, and what is wrong with you (wounds and maiming count against, and carrying only dragonglass makes falling short likelier). Win and he is destroyed; fall short and the knight beside you takes the blow. We do not go to him alone. Form the line. Drafts your companions and opens the Last Hour melee (players only). I have already seen how this goes. The greenseer's option, for a champion with greensight or dragon dreams who also carries a bane: better odds than the blind duel, not a win. Go out there anyway. Somebody has to be first. For a man carrying nothing that can hurt him. He will not kill the Night King today; he walks out, the best knight beside him may die for it, and he is remembered as the Undaunted . Sound the retreat. Not today, and not with this. Live to try again, at 200 prestige. The Last Hour melee A Trial-of-Seven melee in the snow, on the ground the battle was fought on. docs.x: Nobody is born Azor Ahai. You accumulate marks, someone qualified says the name out loud, and then you have to go and do it. Every character in the world is measured the same way, continuously, and the AI competes for the naming as hard as you do. The nine marks Mark How it is decided When Dragon dreams AGOT marks children with it at birth. The mod reads it. Birth Greensight Likewise, and a greenseer can name himself. Birth Born amid salt and smoke Born in a coastal county, while living dragons exist in the world or in a province winter reaches. Common in Aegon's century, rare after the dragons die. Birth Born beneath a bleeding star Born during Winter Is Coming or the Long Night. Birth Hidden blood A bastard of Valyrian descent, not a known dragonseed, whose father held a duchy or better. Birth Valyrian steel A Valyrian sword equipped , not in the vault. Lightbringer counts. Checked live Woke dragons out of stone A dragon bonded to you. Checked live Walked out of a fight with the dead Survive Something Came Out of the Trees yourself, or have your red priest meet them with fire. Earned Died and came back Carry Returned by R'hllor. Earned Read the Signs costs nothing, once a year, and lists the marks on your life. Lose the sword or the dragon and the mark goes with it; a Favored man who drops below the line gets A Faltering Flame and either admits it or keeps the name anyway, at the cost of piety and the temple's patience. Being named Marks alone do nothing. A red priest (your court chaplain with the trait or the faith; a camp priest for the landless), a witch or a greenseer among your courtiers and guests, or your own greensight has to say it. Two marks make you Favored ( A Sword Drawn From Fire : martial +6, prowess +12, stewardship +3, health +2.5, +25 same-faith opinion, +1 piety a month) and four make you Chosen ( The Prince That Was Promised : martial +10, prowess +20, stewardship +6, health +5, +40 same-faith opinion, +2.25 piety a month), each with a twenty-year opinion modifier among the faithful. Under The Flames Are Loud it is one and three; under The Citadel's Reading three and six; Nobody Is Ever Named switches the ladder off. You can accept, accept quietly, or refuse for twenty-five years. Many can be Favored at once, and rival Chosen meet: An Envoy From the Other One can end in friendship and an alliance, a snub, or a challenge. You do not have to be a king; a hedge knight can be named over the head of the man who feeds him. Beneath the naming runs a quieter scoring of destiny : canon and semi-canon characters, Lightbringer, Valyrian steel, the blood of the dragon, dragon dreams and greensight, and a certain kind of hard man in the Long Night all raise it, while contentment, arrogance, cynicism and cowardice lower it. It decides which priests bless whom, and who gets the Last Hour when several could. Lightbringer Two roads, one sword; completing either closes the other for the whole world. docs.x: When the Night King is destroyed, the land the dead held is scoured : the seat of a kingdom becomes a renowned great ruin, the seat of a duchy a sizeable ruin, everything else wilderness. Only counties the mod scoured are ever touched; Harrenhal and the old ruins are left alone. Twenty, thirty or forty-five years later each scoured ruin that nobody has reclaimed becomes wilderness too, so AGOT's own settlement decision can take it. Every player gets A Dream of Spring . The Question of the North goes to the Iron Throne, or an independent King in the North, or the greatest independent crown left standing, within six months: The Watch shall rise again refounds the Night's Watch under a new Lord Commander with the Wall's castles and 500 gold (or reinforces it, if it held), and the free folk are never welcomed south; Let the free folk come south renames the Wall's kingdom the Giftlands and settles it clan by clan, up to two clans a year, as vassals of the crown, and the Watch never rises again. The choice is permanent, even under the Cycle. Lords who fled south as refugees of the Dawn can Return North : a settler caravan with 1,000 provisions and 150 gold, staged up the Kingsroad through King's Landing, the Inn at the Crossroads and Moat Cailin, to their lost seat if it is empty or the nearest empty land. Rebuilding the ancestral seat is worth 200 prestige and Restored the Ancestral Seat for life. A refugee with a dragon can instead Return With Fire and settle the question of who holds his hall; there are four ways that goes and only one of them is quiet. The crown can Sell Colonization Rights to Essos , 150 gold a coastal county to a Braavosi, Pentoshi, Myrish, Tyroshi, Lyseni or Volantene lord, once every eighteen months, and every northern vassal remembers it for ten years. With Iron Throne Reformation on, every independent ruler in the Seven Kingdoms is asked The Future of the Seven Kingdoms : swear fealty to the Iron Throne, or remain independent. Under The Cycle , the Dawn lasts five years and flows back into the Long Summer with the ledger wiped, the Wall raised again and Castle Black repaired, a new summer target rolled, and one thing kept: a Night's Queen survives the cleanup to seed the next wave. Waves two and three carry The Dead Remember (+2 levy size, +3 advantage, +10% toughness), four and five Centuries of Winter (+4, +6, +20% toughness, +10% damage, four knights), six and up The Last Long Night (+7, +10, +35% toughness, +25% damage, eight knights, +25% knight effectiveness). Everyone who stood in the front rank at the last Dawn, and Azor Ahai Reborn, carries Saw the First Dawn when the next night opens, and gets You Have Seen This Before .

docs.x: Compatible with AGOT+, Valyrian Steel, Submod Core, Nobility of Westeros, Essos Expanded, Legacy of Valyria, AGOT Additional Models and Special Buildings, Seasons of Ice and Fire, and anything else that names its own rulers. Supernatural needs the compatibility patch, last in the list. Essos Expanded and Legacy of Valyria are untested and unsupported; keep them above this mod. Legacy of Valyria ships its own versions of three rules this mod overrides, including the one that is the whole entry point to resurrection, so this mod must load after it. Every override is one AGOT or vanilla definition, copied in full, with one documented change, re-checked against the current AGOT build every release: Six scripted rules: alliances (nothing living keeps an alliance with the dead), who may be played (a raised player hands off to an heir; a landed sworn brother is playable), the second chance at death (the last kiss), who may be a guest (not the Others), who may be regent (a sworn brother only for a sworn brother), who may move a camp (ranging captains, and no dragon beyond an intact Wall). Eight scripted triggers: knights, court positions, councillors and commanders (the living do not serve the dead; the Night King leads his own host), capture (he is imprisoned rather than slain in a siege), regency for personal reasons, who may become a landless adventurer (never the dead), and the check thirteen AGOT casus belli share (the dead do not declare war on the dead). Three scripted effects: how rulers are titled (wights, captains and the wilderness get their names; every other mod's titles pass straight through), what happens when a dragon dies in a dragon duel (the dead may claim it), and the melee's scene. One decision, one casus belli, three files: Restore the Night's Watch (hidden once the Question has been asked), the independence war (nobody secedes from the Watch), the ranger-camp domicile (opened to eight companies), the peasant faction (never against a wight), and the portrait animations (five wight poses). Languages: English is complete; the Russian translation covers most of the mod, with the newest events (the Last Hour, the encounter, the spear, consecration, travel danger and a few others) still in English. Large playsets are worth one look at logs/database_conflicts.log .

docs.x: There is a door in this mod. It has no handle on the outside, it opens for one kind of lord, it is checked exactly once, at the moment your character first draws breath, and nobody has ever stumbled into it by accident. Four decisions sit behind it. They do not appear greyed out with their requirements listed; if you are not the one it is waiting for, they do not exist. The riddle of the household ledger Everything you need is below. Nothing below is a lie. Found your own house, and answer to no one above you. Take the sin the septons put in the flesh, and the virtue they put in the work. Both. They sit oddly together. That is rather the point. Then set your sword-arm at three fives , not one more, and not one less. Do all of it in the ruler designer, before the first snow. The door is checked once and never again, so a build that drifts into shape later will find nothing waiting. What's behind it: a household to put in order, a house to write down, a physician worth the name, and a ship that came back from somewhere ships do not come back from. The ship is the big one. No console, no save editing, no downloads. Just a character sheet built a particular way.

docs.x: My priest refused to bring me back. Why? He rolls. The base is 70 to pay against 30 to refuse; if you are not worth the fire (no champion trait, no mark, not fighting in the cold) refusal gets +60, and if you are his friend refusal is cut to a fifth. Make him your friend, earn a mark, and ask again with a fresh priest next time. If the card said there was only ever one of it to give, your priest had already spent his kiss on someone else. I have a red priest but the blessing decision does not show. Check that he is an adult, available (not travelling, not imprisoned), has a first level of devotion or a learning of 10, and has never given the last kiss. Then check that nobody else's blessing already stands over you; the decision tells you if it does. I died and nothing happened. Only battle deaths as a knight or commander, and natural deaths with a red priest as your chaplain, can be argued with. Duels, executions, the Last Hour melee and scripted deaths never can. Battle deaths are also a weighted draw against the game's own, so the blessing raises your odds rather than guaranteeing the card. The Night King took the North and stopped. The North stage waits for the North to be finished, and a northern county held by a vassal of a southern king is not something he can target. The stage times out after twenty years and he moves on. He also never opens a new war while fighting one; before 1.1.1 his own peasant revolts counted, which is fixed. Can I be Lord Commander? Election is AGOT's and the mod does not change who is eligible. A sworn brother holding a castle is playable, and a player Lord Commander who dies passes play to a landed brother of his family. Can a woman take the black? No. The Watch is brothers only, at the gate and in the dungeons order. Does killing him with ordinary steel do anything? It casts him down: another Other is crowned with the same bonuses and the Long Night goes on. It does count as beating the dead, so it opens the War for the Dawn, and you are remembered as the Undaunted. Can I change the rules on an existing save? No. CK3 bakes game rules in when a save is created. Timing, strength, the prophecy coin and the rest need a fresh campaign. Where do I report a bug? The Long Night Discord is fastest; GitHub issues work too. Include your CK3 version, your full load order, and whether you are on the Workshop copy or a manual install.
